concept.title: Read the caller-visible contract
paragraphs: Start with the receiver, input types, return type, and accessibility. A return type promises what a successful caller receives; it does not hide failure meaning.
Use IntelliSense one parameter or member at a time rather than memorizing a dense signature.

lab.title: Choosing Outcome Contracts Across Boundaries
lab.objective: Choose outcome contracts based on what a caller must know at each boundary.
lab.task: Compare inventory lookup, reservation attempts, payment validation, API translation, and UI messaging.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/optional/outcome-contracts from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/optional/outcome-contracts. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/optional/outcome-contracts/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Compare inventory lookup, reservation attempts, payment validation, API translation, and UI messaging.
Step 4/12: Create a scenario table in Program.cs comments covering bool, nullable, result, exception, HTTP status, and UI message.
Step 5/12: Add Product and PaymentResult records as setup below the top-level statements.
Step 6/12: Add FindProduct returning Product? so absence is the entire repository outcome.
Step 7/12: Add TryReserve returning bool for an expected yes/no attempt.
Step 8/12: Add Authorize returning PaymentResult because expected rejection details matter.
Step 9/12: Write one invalid-operation example in comments showing when an exception would protect an object rule.
Step 10/12: Print how repository, service, API, and UI boundaries can translate the same event, then run the project.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/optional/outcome-contracts --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/optional/outcome-contracts --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
